Empower your teams with enterprise search, dynamic artifacts, and cross-tool automation, grounded in business context through Genie Ontology

by Sydney Sundell and Elise Georis

  • One home for AI cowork: Genie One brings Genie Search, organizational directories, and artifacts that stay current to every surface where employees work.
  • From answers to action: Genie One combines an autonomous agent, MCP connections to your SaaS tools, and shareable skills to carry out tasks and work proactively.
  • Control as you scale: Unity Gateway gives admins the traces, MCP policies, and budget controls they need to manage Genie across the organization.

In today’s enterprise, work rarely stays in one application. A single task can involve reconciling a ticket in one system, updating a document in another, and nudging a colleague in a Slack thread while you’re waiting on both. Many of these tools have added their own AI assistants to help you automate and enhance the work you do within them, but they each can help with only its part of the overall task. Without the context of your full workflow and the knowledge spread across the rest of your enterprise, these assistants may speed up individual steps, but you’re still left connecting the pieces and finishing the job by hand.

Earlier this year, we introduced Genie One to help you find insights and automate work. Today, Genie One becomes the enterprise home for AI cowork, where every conversation, artifact, and workflow draws on your enterprise context from Genie Ontology and is governed through Unity Gateway. We also announced today that Genie can now take more autonomous action on your behalf, acting as a true always-on coworker for workflows across teams and tools. This release combines one place for you to find information, build finished work, and act across tools with one unified control plane for admins to govern that work as adoption grows.

Genie One now brings the tools you use to find information, reach colleagues, build finished work and take action into one place.

Genie Search is a new kind of hybrid AI search that unifies context-aware chats, live information retrieval, and enterprise search into one experience. Genie Search starts by creating an index of the knowledge your organization keeps outside Databricks, in documents, tickets and wikis across tools like Google Drive, Jira, Confluence, Workday, and SharePoint. When you ask a question, Genie retrieves from the index to answer quickly and accurately, with fewer tool calls and fewer tokens even while drawing on multiple sources.

Simultaneously, Genie Search supports over 100 MCP connectors, which let Genie retrieve live information and take action, such as checking a Jira ticket’s status or creating one. Genie chooses how to use search, MCP, and SQL for each task based on your query. Indexed content also feeds OntoRank, the method Genie Ontology uses to weigh which sources to trust, so search improves the context behind every answer.

The same index now also powers asset search for items that live outside of Databricks. Sometimes you don’t need a composed answer—just the latest all-hands slides or the ticket for a bug you’re tracking. From the same chat bar where you ask questions and collaborate with Genie today you can now search directly. Results from Google Drive, Jira and Confluence appear alongside Databricks dashboards, tables and Genie Agents, so users can find documents and data in one place.

Genie Search also brings organizational data into both a visible organizational directory and Genie Ontology. In Genie One, you can browse team structures, find the right colleague, and understand reporting relationships. The same data gives Genie Ontology context about people and teams, helping Genie identify more authoritative and relevant sources for its answers.

Admins and users now also have more flexibility over the homepage experience in Genie One, including the ability to pin specific assets such as dashboards, apps, or Genie Agents. Admins can set company-wide pins to bring key updates and resources to the surface, while users can set individual pins based on what they want quick access to from Genie One.

Of course, getting the answer from AI is only half the job. Turning it into a shareable deck, dashboard, or page usually means moving to another tool, and losing context along the way.

Genie One now creates artifacts, including slide decks, dashboards and interactive pages directly in your conversation. You describe the artifact you need, then refine it in collaboration with Genie using the same governed data and context as the conversation. You can inspect the sources behind each number or visualization, check the results, and make changes before sharing, without ever leaving Genie One.

Artifacts also work with scheduled tasks and skills. Scheduled tasks keep the data in an artifact up to date, while skills apply company brand standards.

“With artifacts in Genie, we have full creative control over how we present our data. We can get the exact look and feel we want while keeping everything connected to our governed data — it's the best of both worlds."- Guilherme Vivian, Data Manager, Agibank

Once you’ve worked with Genie to generate insights and artifacts, you can complete your workflow by updating connected tools via MCP connections. Genie One can read and update systems such as Jira or Asana, so the result of an analysis reaches the system of record without you leaving the conversation. Ask Genie to summarize last quarter's open escalations in Jira and post themes to a Slack channel, or to prep for your meetings and find more focus time in your week. You can choose what actions require your approval, and admins can configure which tools they allow their team to connect Genie to.

"Our current safety software is great, but it's limited to what the investigator knows at the time. Genie integrates that safety information with delivery tickets, maintenance records, hours of service, HR, Dispatch, customer information and even the weather! We now get deeper and more complete information about a particular incident and company-wide trends then we ever could before." - Jeff Emrick, Corporate Safety Director, Ozinga

Skills let you capture a workflow once and share it with teammates. Every business team has people who get strong results with AI, whether they're automating a weekly pipeline review or a month-end variance summary. With skills, the rest of the team can run the same steps and get consistent results.

You publish Genie skills to Unity Catalog, where colleagues can find and use them. Each skill runs with the permissions of the person using it, so it accesses only the data and tools that person is authorized to use. Teams can also bring skills built in other AI tools into Genie One and keep their workflows in one place.

Employees move between devices and collaboration tools throughout the day. Genie One is now available through native apps and the AI tools teams already use, with the same governed context and permissions wherever they work.

  • Browser extension: Open Genie One with every new Chrome tab. Install the extension from the Chrome Web Store, and opt in to make Genie One your new-tab page.
  • Desktop apps: Keep Genie One alongside the desktop apps you use throughout the day, with native apps for macOS and Windows. Ask data questions, work with threads and documents, use Genie Agents and Unity Catalog tables, and run Databricks Apps. Desktop features include back and forward navigation, an unread-activity badge, and automatic updates.
  • Mobile apps: Use Genie One on iOS and Android to ask questions, explore and chat with dashboards, and run Databricks Apps. Push notifications let you know when scheduled work is ready, and MCP connections configured on the web carry over to mobile.
  • Slack and Microsoft Teams apps: Message Genie directly or @mention Genie in a channel or group chat. Shared answers give teammates context they can build on, and channel owners can pin a Genie Agent for answers tailored to a specific use case. Genie preserves each user’s identity and permissions, so Genie responds based on the data you are authorized to access. Scheduled work, Skills, and MCP connections configured on the web carry over.
“With Genie One embedded in the flow of work, questions no longer die on the table. An executive can ask something they never would have submitted as a request and get a confident answer before the moment passes.”- Brian Muehlenkamp, Sr. Product Manager, Demand Intelligence,Ticketmaster

In addition to the native Genie One experiences inside of Databricks, you can also access insights from Genie inside any AI cowork tool of your choice. Genie plugins bring Genie into ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot Cowork, and Grok Bot. If you prefer to work in those tools, you get answers grounded in Genie Ontology, with the same Unity Catalog permissions.

However independently an AI coworker acts, people remain accountable for its actions, and that accountability is what lets organizations scale AI confidently. Unity Gateway extends governance from data and context to the actions Genie takes, so admins can see what Genie did, who asked for it and why.

Unity Gateway traces show admins how Genie responded to each request. A trace captures the question, answer, cited objects, response time and actions taken, from running SQL and calling a Genie Agent to publishing a dashboard, scheduling a task or sending a notification. Like audit logs, traces are stored in a table that admins query with their own compute, so they can filter records, join them with other data and build monitoring views.

When a user reports a problem, an admin opens the trace to review the question, SQL, cited objects and thumbs-down feedback. The admin can investigate without a screen share or asking the user to retrace every prompt. Traces also show how Genie is used across the organization, so admins can understand trends and diagnose anomalies over time.

Beyond tracing individual actions, admins can set policies, enforce permissions, and manage costs across Genie One.

  • MCP policies: In Unity Gateway, admins control which MCP servers and tools Genie uses and which actions require human approval.
  • Budgets and cost management: Admins can also use it to review usage, manage budgets, and forecast spending. Genie One is free for users through January 31, 2027. More detailed cost controls will be available before then, giving admins time to plan.

Genie One and Genie Ontology respect Unity Catalog permissions and each connected source's access controls, so users see only information they're authorized to access. When a question needs data a user can't access, Genie can identify the relevant table or asset and prepare an access request for the user to review and submit. Admins review the request in Unity Catalog and grant or decline it. Users get a direct path to the data they need, and access decisions stay with admins.

Genie One gives you one place to find information, create finished work, and take action across tools. Unity Gateway gives admins the visibility and controls to govern that work as adoption grows.

Visit our documentation for up-to-date availability of the features outlined above, or contact your Databricks account team for more information.

  • Admins: Enable Genie tracing in Unity Gateway, review MCP policies, and connect your first sources through Genie Search. 
  • Business users: Open Genie One, search across your tools, and ask it to build your next dashboard or deck. Save what works as a skill and share it with your team. For more inspiration, visit our Genie at Work demo library. 

To learn more about taking action on your unified context layer, register for Data and AI Live: Context is just the beginning with Ali Ghodsi and Greg Brockman.

Genie One is the Databricks enterprise home for AI cowork, where business users search company knowledge, analyze data, build finished work and take action across their tools. It draws on business context from Genie Ontology and is governed by Unity Gateway.

Yes. It combines an autonomous agent, MCP connections, scheduled tasks and shareable skills to carry out multistep work across tools, like summarizing Jira escalations and posting the themes to Slack. You choose which actions need your approval.

Yes. Genie Search indexes knowledge from tools like Google Drive, Jira, Confluence, Workday and SharePoint, and uses more than 100 MCP connectors for live lookups. Results appear next to Databricks dashboards, tables and Genie Agents.

You ask in plain language, and Genie writes and runs the SQL on governed data, then returns tables, charts and citations. Genie Ontology tells it which sources your team trusts, so it doesn't have to guess.

Look for business context, the ability to act, governance and reach. Genie One covers all four: Genie Ontology for context, MCP actions and artifacts for action, Unity Gateway for governance, and native apps for reach.

Yes. It respects Unity Catalog permissions and each connected source's access controls, so users see only what they're allowed to see. Admins use Unity Gateway to set MCP policies, require approvals and trace what Genie does.

Yes. It updates tools like Jira and Asana through MCP and has native Slack and Microsoft Teams apps. MCP plugins bring it into ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot Cowork, and Grok Bot., with the same context and permissions everywhere.

Business users get governed answers themselves, right in their own tools. Scheduled tasks and shared skills turn recurring requests into automatic, consistent workflows.

Genie Ontology learns your definitions, metrics and business rules from the assets your teams already use, and ranks them by how authoritative they are. Certifying key metrics in Unity Catalog makes it more accurate.

Admins monitor usage and manage budgets in Unity Gateway. Genie One is free for users through January 31, 2027, and more detailed cost controls will be available before then.

entries.content:
The agentic ontology, built by agents, governed by people, and designed for every agent, is now Generally Available with expanded knowledge sources and new tools to curate and refine it.

by Ken Wong, Paul Roome and Richard Tomlinson

  • Genie Ontology, now Generally Available, is an agentic ontology that agents build from your teams' everyday work and people govern, giving every agent one understanding of the business.
  • This release introduces Genie Search for enterprise knowledge, extends learned context to BI tools and organizational directories, adds Ontology Manager for curation and brings Unity Catalog Domains and Pages to General Availability.
  • In a benchmark built with Turing, Genie with Genie Ontology passed 91% of enterprise task runs, 1.6× the rate of the strongest frontier agent, while using less than half the tokens.

AI agents are only as useful as their understanding of the business in which they work. Within a given domain, teams can curate that understanding by hand. Thousands of customers now run Genie Agents in production this way, including 7-Eleven, Virgin Atlantic and General Motors. However, enterprises are no longer deploying a single agent for a single domain. They are deploying many agents across every function, and each needs the same accurate and complete understanding of how the business works.

The enterprise context that agents need is far larger than any team can write down or model by hand. It lives in the logic behind thousands of production dashboards, SQL queries, notebooks and BI semantic models, as well as in the documents and applications where teams record definitions and maintain a working knowledge of who does what. It also changes every week as products launch, campaigns run, and teams reorganize.

This is why ontologies have historically struggled in the enterprise. Built by specialists and maintained manually, they captured only a narrow slice of the business and quickly became outdated as the business evolved. Agents change both sides of that problem. They are now the primary consumers of enterprise context, and they can also produce it by learning from the work teams already do. The result is a new kind of agentic ontology, built by agents, used by agents and governed by the people who know the business.

We believe every organization will need a single agentic ontology that connects to all of its data, learns continuously from how the business operates and gives every agent the same governed understanding, whether it runs on Databricks or elsewhere. Building context, agent by agent, produces separate and partial views of the business, and those views inevitably conflict. An enterprise ontology should therefore be shared infrastructure that IT and data leaders own in the same way they own the data platform beneath it.

At Data + AI Summit, we introduced Genie Ontology as that layer. Today, we're announcing its General Availability, with new sources for agents to learn from and new tools for people to curate and govern what they learn. We're also sharing results from a benchmark developed with Turing that show how much more accurately agents work when they draw on it.

Genie Ontology is agentic because agents continuously build its knowledge for other agents to use, while people govern the business definitions that require precision. It combines learned and modeled knowledge, ranks it by authority, and delivers the most trusted context to agents while respecting existing user permissions.

Most of Genie Ontology's knowledge is automatically learned from the systems and artifacts that reflect how an organization operates. Agents extract business context from the assets teams already work with, including Databricks dashboards, SQL queries, notebooks and semantic models in tools like Power BI. This knowledge is captured as Ontology Snippets, reusable pieces of business context such as calculations, business rules, and data relationships, which are continuously updated as the underlying sources evolve. By learning directly from everyday work, Genie Ontology grows more useful over time and captures the long tail of team-specific knowledge that would be impractical to model and maintain manually.

Learned knowledge is complemented by modeled knowledge, which is the business meaning teams define explicitly and govern through Unity Catalog semantics. This includes Metric Views that hold certified KPIs, Domains that organize knowledge by business area and Pages that record authoritative definitions of business concepts. Organizations model the comparatively small set of definitions that must be exact, such as recognized revenue or ARR, and Genie Ontology treats those definitions as the source of truth wherever they apply.

When an agent asks a question, OntoRank, Genie Ontology's authority-aware ranking algorithm, evaluates learned and modeled knowledge to identify the most trustworthy context. It weighs signals such as source authority, certification, the expertise and relevance of the people behind the knowledge, popularity, and recency to resolve conflicting definitions and select the best context for each user and question. Genie Ontology then delivers that context directly to the agent, which can reason from the correct definitions immediately rather than spending time and tokens on open-ended exploration of the data.

Through Genie MCP, the same context is available to agents outside Databricks, such as ChatGPT, Claude and Microsoft Copilot, so the agents teams already use become smarter about the business without being rebuilt.

The clearest test of an agentic ontology is whether agents that draw on it outperform those that must find context on their own. Existing data agent benchmarks focus mostly on tables, and frontier agents now score similarly on them, even though real enterprise questions often depend on business context that is fragmented across notebooks, dashboards and documents. To better approximate the real world, we worked with Turing to build a new benchmark simulating a live, realistic Databricks workspace for a fictional UK energy supplier. It compares Genie, powered by Genie Ontology, with two leading frontier agents, labeled Agent A and Agent B. Every agent answered the same questions five times per task, and each answer was graded against a rubric defined before the runs began.

Agent

Genie answered correctly in 91% of runs, 1.6 times the rate of the stronger frontier agent, while using less than half the tokens and finishing three to four times faster. Because all three agents write SQL well, the difference comes from context. Genie drew on knowledge the Ontology had already learned from the workspace and went directly to the business rules each question required, while the frontier agents had to rediscover that knowledge on every run and frequently returned answers that failed to meet those rules. The results reflect an established deployment where teams have accumulated that knowledge, and the benchmark research blog covers the methodology and task walkthroughs. Your account team can help you run the same evaluation in your own workspace.

An agentic ontology can learn only from data its agents can reach, so a context layer for the whole enterprise depends on connecting to a wide variety of sources. Structured data either enters Unity Catalog via Lakeflow Connect or is federated in place, so Genie can compute answers directly from live operational data. Much of what a business knows, however, lives outside the lakehouse in the documents, tickets and wikis where teams record decisions and explain how things work. With this release, we are significantly expanding the systems the Ontology connects to.

Genie Search, now Generally Available, lets people and agents find and use enterprise knowledge in documents, tickets and wikis alongside their governed Databricks assets, within the permissions they already have. Users can find documents anywhere in the enterprise or ask questions that span many of them at once. Genie returns synthesized, cited answers alongside the dashboards, tables and Genie Agents they already use. Because indexed content also informs OntoRank, the knowledge in those documents and tickets becomes part of the evidence Genie Ontology weighs when deciding which sources to trust.

To configure Genie Search, through the admin console, an administrator connects each source and enables indexing. 

Genie can then search the full index in a single pass rather than querying each source separately, making answers more complete and enabling agents to find the right information with fewer tool calls and tokens. For real-time work, such as checking a Jira ticket status or creating a new one, Genie Search works alongside MCP connectors. Genie decides for each task how much to draw on the index, MCP or SQL. Genie Search supports Google Drive, Jira, Confluence and Workday today, with SharePoint in Beta and many more connectors coming soon.

Recreating and maintaining source permissions is one of the most difficult parts of deploying enterprise search. Genie Search ingests each source's access controls alongside its content through Unity Catalog connections and enforces them before returning any result, so people and agents see only what they could already open in the original application. Because Genie Search runs as a managed service on Databricks, organizations do not need to maintain a separate permission model or procure separate search infrastructure. Genie Search is available today in Genie and for asset search on the Discover page.

Learned knowledge is the largest part of Genie Ontology, and with this release it extends beyond the workspace into external BI tools and the organizational relationships that determine whose knowledge is most relevant to each person.

Ontology Snippets, now Generally Available, are the units that make up Genie Ontology's learned knowledge. Genie builds them automatically and continuously from the dashboards, SQL queries and notebooks people already use and refreshes them as that work changes, so the Ontology keeps pace with the business without anyone maintaining it by hand. Each snippet stays tied to the asset it came from and inherits that asset's permissions, which means Genie draws only on context the user is already allowed to see. When Genie cites a snippet, users can see where the definition came from, who authored it and why it was trusted.

Much of an organization's business logic already lives in the semantic models of BI tools such as Power BI, Tableau and Sigma, and rebuilding it for every AI initiative duplicates work and creates context drift. External knowledge sources, now in Beta, bring that logic into Genie Ontology by connecting to external BI platforms, identifying semantic models, measures, calculated columns and relationships, and generating Ontology Snippets from them. Power BI is supported today. Tableau and Sigma support is coming soon, and lineage support will follow. To get started, review the product documentation.

Business knowledge is only half the picture. To make it useful, agents also need to understand the people behind it and how they relate to the person asking. Organizational directories, now Generally Available, bring this context into Genie Ontology. Starting with Workday, they import people, teams and reporting relationships, making them accessible through a people browser in Genie.

Genie Ontology combines these formal organizational relationships with activity signals that reveal who actually works together through the assets they create, share and use. OntoRank uses both to give greater weight to knowledge from teammates and close collaborators, helping agents deliver answers that are more relevant to each user.

Genie Ontology continuously learns and improves through usage, but the quality of an agent's answers still depends on the accuracy of the knowledge it relies on. That's why organizations need the ability to review, refine, and govern their ontology. Databricks provides these capabilities within the same platform that governs the underlying data, ensuring agents operate on trusted business context.

Governance builds on the controls organizations already use across Databricks. Unity Catalog governs the underlying knowledge, managing permissions, lineage, and definitions to ensure users and agents access only what they're authorized to see. Unity Gateway governs how agents interact with that knowledge, controlling connections, usage limits, guardrails, and auditing. Together, they provide consistent governance as Genie Ontology extends to more agents and systems, without introducing a separate control plane.

Domains and subdomains, now Generally Available, give Genie Ontology its organizational structure. They group data and AI assets by their business purpose, so when the same term means different things to different teams, Genie can apply the definition that best fits the question based on its associated domain. Domains also enable people to browse and find data on the Discover page, based on how their business is organized. Curation and management can be delegated at the domain or subdomain level, so Finance and Marketing can each maintain their own definitions and assets without relying on a central team.

“Making data easier to discover and understand is an important part of how we're evolving our analytics capabilities across the Airline. Databricks Domains gives us a clearer, more intuitive way to organize our data, helping our teams navigate an increasingly complex data landscape with greater confidence.”- Tom Barber, Head of BI & Advanced Analytics, Virgin Atlantic
“Domains and subdomains make it simple for business users to locate and gain access to data assets needed in their business role."- Michael Poremba, Senior Manager, Data Architecture, McAfee

Unity Catalog Pages, now Generally Available, provide your authoritative definitions to Genie Ontology. Each Page is a governed explanation of a business term, entity or acronym, with a named owner and a home in a domain or subdomain. When a question involves a defined concept, Genie treats the Page as the source of truth, preferring it over learned context, and cites it so users can verify the answer.

Agents can help create Pages as well as consume them. Teams can use the "Bulk import Pages" prompt in Genie Code to draft Pages from MCP-connected tools such as Confluence, Slack, Google Docs and GitHub, or use the public API to sync with existing knowledge platforms. Pages link directly to Unity Catalog assets, dashboards and other Pages, and each one remains under the control of its named owner.

"What used to take me two weeks at a previous job, I can now do in five minutes. With Unity Catalog Pages, Genie understands how Agrifirm defines active and inactive customers and calculates inactivity windows, making complex historical analyses faster and more transparent. By showing the methodology behind the numbers, Genie helps us build trust in its answers upfront." - Henri van Dijk, Data Governance and Quality Assurance Officer, Agrifirm
"With Unity Catalog Pages, we can give our Genie Agents a trusted source of business knowledge that is prioritized by Ontology and results in much better answers to very specific questions. And because we're using Pages to define industry terms and acronyms, each agent's instructions can be much more streamlined, resulting in better working memory - and again - better answers."- Ian Smith, Databricks Platform Manager, Waste Connections

As agents add to the Ontology, the people responsible for it need a way to see what it knows, find where it falls short and curate the knowledge that matters most. Ontology Manager, coming soon in Beta, will be the first visual interface for this work. Data stewards and context engineers will assess the overall health of the Ontology, identify the most significant gaps, set the top-level domain structure and configure external knowledge sources. Domain experts will organize and curate knowledge within their business area, and business users will be able to see the context Genie draws on within their existing permissions.

Ontology Manager will also surface high-impact opportunities, such as domains where coverage is thin or frequently asked concepts that lack governed definitions, and stewards will be able to promote what agents have learned into authoritative Pages directly from a review queue. An interactive graph will let users explore the entities and relationships within Genie Ontology and create new knowledge, while a hierarchical view will support day-to-day curation within a specific domain. To learn more about Ontology Manager, watch the product demo.

"We value that Genie Ontology makes the context behind answers more transparent and inspectable; citations let people trace answers to the underlying sources and business definitions, which helps build trust and improve the experience for our stakeholders.”- Jehan Saga, Manager of Data Engineering, Superhuman
"Genie Ontology is exactly what we need to scale AI without losing the business context that makes it useful. It's a force multiplier for our data teams." - Noah Cepela, SVP, Analytics and Insights, Mode Global
"Databricks Ontology with Genie Code has been a game changer for us. We're using it to build dashboards, apps, AI agents, and more. Power BI reports that used to take days to create can now be built in hours with Genie Code, and our analysts are so excited by the experience that they're already looking to move more of their reporting to Databricks Dashboards. The impact goes well beyond reporting: analysts who previously worked primarily in Excel and SQL are now using Genie Code to build Databricks Apps that support our operational teams. By putting that capability directly in the hands of analysts, we've been able to deliver solutions much faster and save our operational teams over 1000 manhours every month."- Kyle Burke, VP, Data Platform, BHG Financial
“Business semantics have made our Genie experiences more accurate and context-aware across Genie, Agent and Code. Instead of embedding business knowledge into individual agents through skills and instructions, we can establish it once and make it available across solutions and domains.”- Kristoffer Absalonsen, Enterprise Architect, Odfjell Technology
“At Zepto, we want AI to understand how our business works, not just the data it processes. Genie Ontology helps us do this by bringing business definitions and context together. For instance, metrics like order fulfillment time, delivery TAT and fill rate are meaningful only when understood in the right business context. This helps AI go beyond reporting metrics to interpreting them and turning business data into actionable insights.”- Deepak Siroya, VP of Analytics, Zepto

Genie Ontology is Generally Available today. Organizations can start with the context they already have, governing the definitions that matter most in Unity Catalog and letting Genie Ontology learn the rest from the work their teams do every day. To learn more:

  • Join us for the Data + AI Live: Context is just the beginning event with Ali Ghodsi and Greg Brockman 
  • Explore the Genie Ontology product page
  • Read the Genie Ontology documentation
  • Download the eBook Operationalizing the Enterprise Context Layer
  • Watch the new Genie Ontology Manager demo video

This is one of many announcements during our Week of Genie. Over the coming days, we will share what is new across Genie, Genie Agents and Genie MCP, all of which are built on the agentic ontology introduced here.

We can't wait to see how Genie Ontology helps you deploy reliable AI agents across your entire enterprise.

Genie Agents now reason across your Lakehouse data, unstructured documents and enterprise tools in a single conversation.

by Hanlin Sun and Nikhil Gangaraju

  • Analyze unstructured data: Ask questions across governed tables and thousands of documents in Unity Catalog volumes, with page-level citations. Now in Public Preview.
  • Connect and take action: Pull in app data with Lakeflow and use native MCP connectors (now GA) to read from tools like Jira, Slack and Google Drive and act on them.
  • Share beyond your company: Use OpenSharing (beta) and Genie Clean Rooms (beta) to give partners and customers a governed agent without exposing the data behind it.

Thousands of teams use Genie Agents to turn deep operational questions into actionable outcomes every day. Across industries, organizations are putting Genie Agents to work on some of their most important business challenges:

  • Retail and consumer goods: Unilever uses Genie Agents to help finance teams explore profitability, credit risk and financial performance in natural language. HelloFresh uses Genie Agents to increase ad-testing velocity by 4x by unifying marketing performance insights across media, creative and finance teams.
  • Energy: S&P Global Energy uses Genie Agents to bring new data products to market in days, rather than through traditional development cycles. Its domain experts publish governed, conversational access to commodity data themselves, from LNG cargoes to chemical capacity. Customers can query that data directly from their own AI agents.
  • Technology: Atlassian uses Genie Agents to help security teams investigate billions of security events through natural language, accelerating threat hunting and incident response.
  • Automotive: General Motors has deployed over 1000 Genie agents across sales teams, automotive engineers, supply chain specialists, HR operations, and more, all grounded in the specific context of each line of business.
  • Healthcare and life sciences: ModMed uses Genie Agents to give nontechnical teams secure, natural language access to enterprise data, using catalog structure, permissions and business context to answer questions without requiring a custom AI application for every request.

What these use cases have in common is the need for agents that deeply understand each business's unique context. Genie Agents ground their responses and actions in rich knowledge curated within Databricks, helping teams move from natural-language questions to trusted insights and action.

As demand for context-rich workflows grows, agents need to reason beyond structured business data alone. They need to understand context from unstructured assets and connect to enterprise tools so they can reason across the full business environment and take action in the tools that run their business.

Genie Agents started as the fastest way to turn business questions into SQL insights. Today, they have evolved into something bigger: a no-code agent that understands your entire business context. With unstructured data analysis and new MCP connectors, Genie Agents can conduct high-quality business analytics, analyze large volumes of documents and connect to your enterprise tools to take action on your behalf.

And now with support for OpenSharing, Genie Agents can accelerate time-to-insights outside your enterprise. You can share a governed agent that's pre-loaded with your data, instructions and knowledge with partners, suppliers and customers. External teams can immediately use Genie Agents to get value out of your data, without spending time cross-collaborating on insights.

Genie Clean Rooms go further, offering privacy-centric agentic collaboration. Your recipients get a Genie Agent to chat with your data. But the underlying dataset and IP are hidden and fully protected. These updates let you extend governed Genie Agents to every stakeholder in your ecosystem.

80% of the context that runs an enterprise lives in documents: contracts, invoices, claims, medical records, financial reports and call transcripts. Unlocking this context at scale can transform your business.

Most agents today rely on basic enterprise search via MCP connectors, which let you attach a handful of documents directly and pull out the raw text as context in the session. However, many enterprise use cases involve large document corpora or complex file structures. Maintaining context and compliance here requires understanding the document structure and its relationships while creating a secure perimeter for governing enterprise data.

Building these workflows at scale also requires developing custom RAG, including advanced parsing capabilities, building a separate AI Search endpoint, writing an embedding pipeline, summarizing document insights and passing those summaries to a supervisor agent framework with robust permissions.

A bespoke approach to large-scale unstructured analysis can therefore quickly become expensive to build and maintain.

Genie Agents simplify unstructured data work for your team by automatically handling document parsing, indexing and context retrieval to return high-quality results along with specific citations.

Genie Agents use our custom AI document parsing function to read each file the way a person would. They recognize tables, figures, headers and footers and preserve the surrounding context. Because parsing and indexing run at scale, one agent can work through thousands of files, searching for the ones relevant to your question and citing the exact page for each answer.

What’s powerful about doing this in Genie Agents is that users can now ask questions that span files and tables. “Customers like Verana Health leverage Databricks today to process and analyze real-world clinical data at scale, generating meaningful insights from their healthcare datasets using Genie Agents.

“Our team is now looking to expand these capabilities with Genie Agents to unlock insights from unstructured clinical data and other clinical documents. We're excited about the potential to make this information more accessible through natural language, enabling our teams to explore richer clinical insights alongside structured data.”- Vinodh Simon, Director of Engineering, Verana Health

Let's look at a few additional examples.

Combining quantitative and qualitative insights across tables and files.

An investment analyst sees that a portfolio company's margin has declined for three consecutive quarters. That evidence might exist in analyst reports, earnings call transcripts and industry research PDFs. A Genie Agent pulls margin and selling-price trends from governed tables to find which product lines account for the decline. It then searches the attached analyst reports and earnings transcripts for what competitors did over the same quarters. Genie provides analysts with data trends, the likely causes and page-level citations for each claim.

Answering questions with files as cited references.

In many businesses, users need to complete a task and need guidance from internal documents. The fix might be in one of thousands of service manuals, bulletins and troubleshooting guides, which cover different models and revisions. In this example, the agent identifies the model, searches only the relevant manuals and service bulletins out of thousands of documents and returns the troubleshooting steps with a citation to the source page. AI parsing keeps tables, diagrams and numbered steps intact, so the technician gets the whole procedure.

Analyze data patterns and trends across files.

Sometimes users need qualitative analysis across multiple unstructured files. A clinical trial analyst notices in the trial-tracking data that one department is running fewer studies. The reasons may be written in investigator and doctor reports, spread across dozens of PDFs. The agent confirms the trend in the trial data, then reads that department's doctor reports and pulls out the reasons that keep coming up. Each one is cited back to the source, so the analyst can check the evidence before acting. Reading those reports one by one might take days.

Agent builders can attach Unity Catalog Volumes containing PDFs, documents, slide decks or images directly to a Genie Agent. The agent retrieves the file content most relevant to the question and adds it to its context. The agent then reasons over that content together with any structured data to generate an answer with citations. These citations can point to the specific page of the source file. Users can ask questions across a specific volume, multiple volumes and structured data in the same conversation.

Unstructured data analysis runs in Agent mode, using multi-step reasoning to retrieve and analyze the most relevant file content. It respects Unity Catalog permissions, meaning users only see files they have access to, and supports content search indexing for faster, higher-quality retrieval across large volumes of data.

Genie Agents now give you more ways to connect business context across your systems and tools

Bring structured data in with Lakeflow Connect. Lakeflow Connect lets you ingest data from apps like Salesforce, Workday, SAP or Marketo into Unity Catalog. Once in the Lakehouse, Genie Agents analyze it as accurately as any other governed table, using your curated metric views

Take action with MCP connectors. Native MCP connectors, now GA, let agents get context from tools like Slack, Google Drive, Google Calendar, Gmail, Glean, Atlassian, Github and Microsoft 365. Genie Agents can also act by creating tickets, updating records and posting messages. Authors can choose exactly which tools each agent can use, and every connector is governed through Unity Gateway.

Structured data, documents and tools sit under the same governance, so one agent can reason across all three and take action on those insights

Take a sales team getting ready for a quarterly pipeline review. A Genie agent analyzes pipeline data in Databricks, pulls in account plans from Google Drive and win-loss reports from UC volumes, then posts a deal strategy summary to the team's Slack channel. Agent authors can limit the Slack connector to posting summaries only, and admins govern every connection through Unity Gateway. That turns hours of manual prep into an automated workflow that keeps the whole team aligned.

“Teams make their best decisions when trusted context shows up in the flow of work. With Genie Agents now connected to Slack, sales, finance and operations teams can go from question to action without leaving the conversation. We’re thrilled to work alongside Databricks to bring governed, reliable insights to where the work happens.”- Jaime DeLanghe, Chief Product Officer, Slack

With OpenSharing for Genie Agents, a provider can now share a fully functional Genie Agent with an external recipient, pre-loaded with instructions and context, across Databricks accounts. Under the hood, OpenSharing provides live access to the underlying data. This opens up use cases for data monetization, partner collaboration and cross-org analytics without giving up control of your data infrastructure. Customers or data partners can sell "data intelligence” through packaged agents in the Databricks Marketplace alongside data providers such as FactSet or LSEG and monetize this with their customers.

For sharing use cases that require privacy protection, such as sensitive healthcare or financial data, Genie Clean Rooms let you share an agent where the recipient can ask questions and get answers, but cannot see the underlying data or your IP. This opens up exciting new possibilities for data sharing, where data previously too sensitive to share in its entirety may now be sanitized and shared. Genie Clean Room also offers additional controls, such as conversation limits and output size controls, so you stay in control of your data and how recipients use it.

Genie Agents are accurate because they understand your business, not just your schema. Every agent is grounded in the enterprise context layer that learns your business definitions, metrics, table relationships and column meanings. Subject matter experts then add to that context in three ways:

  • Metric views define each business metric once in Unity Catalog. The agent reads its measures, dimensions, descriptions and synonyms directly.
  • SQL expressions and example queries set joins, measures and filters. When someone asks about "active customers," the agent uses your definition and joins the right tables on the first try.
  • Instructions cover terminology and rules specific to your organization, such as how sales tells committed accounts apart from prospects.

Benchmarks make Agents more reliable over time. They work like unit tests: you define your most common questions with gold-standard SQL answers, score the agent and rerun after changes to catch regressions. Genie suggests fixes such as missing joins, filters or descriptions. In production, the monitoring tab and user feedback show where answers fall short, so the agent improves with use.

The next wave of agents won't wait for someone to open a chat. They'll monitor pipelines, triage escalations, review at-risk deals and answer partners’ questions around the clock. An agent working on its own needs more context, your metrics, your terminology and the guardrails to do its job.

Genie Agents are built for this work. They can be scoped for a business domain or workflow with its own data, files, tools and instructions. Teams can define this agent once, then deploy it through APIs, custom applications and automated workflows. Genie One and Genie MCP can also call these agents when a task needs deeper investigation.

Each agent you build also adds context that the rest of the company can use. A metric defined for finance is available when sales builds its agent, and a correction from one team can become a governed definition for everyone. You don't have to finish mapping the business before you put agents to work, because building context and deploying agents feed each other.

This week's launches expand all three parts of that work. Genie Agents can now reason over thousands of documents alongside governed tables, take action in the tools your teams already use and serve partners and customers outside your company, with your governance applied throughout.

For more information, review these resources:

  • How to choose your first Genie Agents for maximum impact — a scoring framework for picking the right first use case
  • Best Practice for Building Genie Agents — best practices from data prep to production
  • Genie Agents documentation — setup guides, API reference, and configuration details

What’s new in Databricks Genie Agents?

Genie Agents can now analyze unstructured files in Unity Catalog volumes, connect to enterprise tools and be shared outside your company. Unstructured data analysis is in Public Preview, native MCP connectors are generally available, and OpenSharing and Genie Clean Rooms for Genie Agents are in beta.

How do Genie Agents analyze unstructured documents?

Agent builders attach Unity Catalog volumes that contain PDFs, documents, slide decks or images to a Genie Agent. The agent retrieves the most relevant file content, reasons over it together with structured data and answers with citations that can point to the specific page of the source file. It respects Unity Catalog permissions, so users only see files they have access to.

Which enterprise tools can Genie Agents connect to?

Lakeflow Connect ingests data from apps like Salesforce, Workday, SAP or Marketo into Unity Catalog, where Genie Agents analyze it like any other governed table. Native MCP connectors let agents get context from tools like Jira, Confluence, Slack, Google Drive and Microsoft 365, and act by creating tickets, updating records and posting messages. Authors choose which tools each agent can use, and every connector is governed through Unity Gateway.

Can I share a Genie Agent with partners or customers outside my company?

Yes. With OpenSharing, a provider can share a fully functional Genie Agent, pre-loaded with instructions and context, with an external recipient across Databricks accounts. For sensitive data, Genie Clean Rooms let recipients ask questions and get answers without seeing the underlying data or your IP, with controls such as conversation limits and output size limits.

How do Genie Agents stay accurate?

Genie Agents are grounded in an enterprise context layer that learns your business definitions, metrics, table relationships and column meanings. Subject matter experts add metric views, SQL expressions and example queries, and instructions. Benchmarks work like unit tests to catch regressions, and the monitoring tab and user feedback show where answers fall short.

Databricks Genie plugins connect the agents your teams use to business context, leveraging Genie’s trusted insights and ontology

by Ben Tripp and Nikhil Gangaraju

  • Databricks Genie plugins work natively in ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot Cowork and Grok Bot. Agents without a native plugin can reach Genie through the MCP server.
  • Agents draw on Genie Ontology for certified definitions and relationships. Genie writes and runs the SQL over data the user is allowed to see and returns answers with citations.
  • Agents can hand a business question to Genie to investigate, or pull in the context they're missing while they edit files, draft plans or post to Slack.

Every business is adding more data to their AI-powered workflows. But more data doesn't automatically mean better insights. Inevitably, it means more places for an agent to look and more chances to find the wrong answer. Ask a frontier agent a question about your business and it starts a live search. It hops between MCP servers, opens a document, reads a schema, tries a table, backs out and tries another. It has little context on where the right answer lives, so it may guess its way through a random walk across the organization's data.

What agents need is a map of the business before they start looking. That's why we announced Genie Ontology, the enterprise context layer, that combines governed definitions with continuously learned organizational knowledge giving AI agents the business understanding they need to deliver trusted insights.

Today we are introducing new Databricks Genie plugins that give your team’s favorite agents a governed interface to access your enterprise context. These plugins work natively today in ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot Cowork and Grok Bot so teams can maintain business context in Databricks and make it available across their preferred agents.

Frontier agents can now draw on Genie Ontology to supply the definitions, relationships, and source context needed to interpret the business. Genie works out what the business terms mean, finds the right data across tables and documents, writes and runs SQL and returns an answer with citations to its sources.

For questions requiring specialized analysis, Genie can route work to domain-specific Genie Agents. A question about pipeline attribution routes to the marketing Genie Agent. A question about operational costs routes to the finance Genie Agent. Genie also supports insights from unstructured data so teams can access insights from large volumes of unstructured data that reside inside their enterprise

For clients that support the MCP Apps extension, Genie returns interactive visualizations and Genie Ontology citations directly in the conversation. You see the charts, sources, and definitions without leaving your workflow.

Some requests are complex business related questions: why is activation tracking low? Which accounts are at risk and why? The agent infers that the question belongs to Genie and hands it over. Genie then runs its own loop:

  • It works out what the business terms mean using Genie Ontology.
  • It finds data the user is allowed to see and runs It writes and runs the SQL,
  • it routes to a domain Genie Agent if needed for further investigation.
  • It returns an answer with citations.

Other times the agent owns a bigger job, like changing codebase, or monitoring a new product release. Here the agent checks for the business context it's missing and then keeps going with its own tools: editing files, drafting a plan, posting to Slack.



Lets see a few examples of this in action:

Dots are always-on agents in ChatGPT with its own computer that keeps working between conversations. A product manager can give a dot a standing job: watch the launch of a new feature and flag anything that needs attention. Each morning the dot asks Genie how adoption is tracking, using the certified definition of an active user, and checks it against launch targets. When a segment slips, it pulls related support themes and posts a short summary to the team's Slack channel.

A product manager might ask their dot:

  • Track weekly adoption of the new feature against target, by plan tier
  • Engage accounts tried the feature once and never came back
  • Investigate drop in enterprise usage after last Tuesday's release

Claude is built for long, agentic work across many sources. With the Genie plugin, Claude can check important facts before it draws any conclusions. Say a business analyst has to explain why quarterly revenue in a given region came in 10% below forecast. Claude can ask Genie for revenue, order volume and average deal size by product and channel, using the certified metric definitions finance relies on. It then has Genie search pricing memos, sales call notes and competitor reports for what changed during the quarter. From there, Claude goes through a deep analysis with citations behind each claim and totals that match the official forecast.

A business analyst might ask:

  • Why did Northeast revenue miss forecasts last quarter? Back it up with our sales and competitor data.
  • Which products and channels drove most of the gap, and was it fewer orders or smaller deals?
  • Write the variance summary for the QBR using our certified revenue metric

Microsoft Copilot Cowork: Automate account planning with governed data

Microsoft Copilot Cowork automates agentic work across Microsoft 365. It plans multi-step work, runs it in the background, and hands back finished spreadsheets, decks and email drafts. With the Azure Databricks Genie plugin, Cowork can now help an account team prepare for a client meeting. Through Genie, Cowork can pull usage and account trends from Azure Databricks, using governed and certified metric definitions. From there it fills in the account team's briefing template in Word, builds an Excel overview with charts, and creates a client-ready presentation. Cowork also books the client call with the account update, then waits for approval before anything is sent.

An account director might ask:

  • Prep me for this week's customer meetings with a brief on usage, spend against commit, and open escalations.
  • Build the slides for Thursday's business review using our certified consumption metrics
  • After each meeting, use the Teams recap to draft an Outlook follow-up with the numbers we discussed

Grok Bot: Hire an AI teammate to run your growth campaigns end to end

Grok Bot gives your team always-on AI teammates. Each one has its own role, memory and tools, and its own cloud computer that stays on. You can hire a growth marketing teammate and give it a job, and it proactively runs the workflow on a schedule without being prompted. With Genie connected, it works from the campaign spend, qualified opportunity and pipeline definitions your company already governs in Databricks, so its numbers match the ones your team reports.

Every week, the teammate runs the whole campaign review loop. It asks Genie which campaigns are missing targets, digs into why, and drafts budget shifts with the evidence attached. It also pulls product-usage and CRM data to build re-engagement audiences. Your growth lead reviews and approves, and the teammate then sets up the retargeting or lifecycle campaigns in your connected ad tools. One person's weekly analysis can become a workflow that runs itself.

Jobs a bot teammate might take on:

  • Every Monday, find the three campaigns with the highest cost per qualified opportunity, recommend budget changes
  • Build a re-engagement shortlist of accounts whose usage dropped more than 30% over the last 28 days.
  • Find the campaigns that are behind their quarterly targets, work out the gaps, and draft an action plan

Genie plugins extend the same governed business context through our Genie MCP server into AI assistants, coding agents, and client interfaces. Genie Ontology is the governed context layer in Databricks that helps Genie understand your business. Together, they allow organizations to build business meaning once in Genie Ontology and access it across an evolving AI ecosystem. Organizations can also leverage the MCP server directly in your tools to access insights from Genie

Enable the Databricks Genie plugin in your agent workspace. Once connected, start asking business questions in your normal workflow or assigning tasks to your agents. Genie handles the data retrieval and governance. Agents without native plugins can also access Genie via the MCP server.

Join us for the Data + AI Live: Context is just the beginning event with Ali Ghodsi and Greg Brockman to learn more about how Databricks is powering the enterprise context for your agents.

For more information, review these resources:

  • Genie One MCP documentation
  • Genie One MCP: Give any AI Agent the Right Business Context
  • Operationalizing Genie Ontology in Your Data Stack

What are Databricks Genie plugins?

Databricks Genie plugins give the AI agents your teams already use a governed interface to your enterprise context in Databricks. They work natively in ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot Cowork and Grok Bot. Agents without a native plugin can access Genie through the MCP server.

How do AI agents use the Genie plugin?

Agents use it in two ways. They can hand off a business question, and Genie works out what the terms mean using Genie Ontology, finds data the user is allowed to see, writes and runs the SQL and returns an answer with citations. Or the agent keeps the job and asks Genie only for the business context it's missing, then continues with its own tools.

What does Genie Ontology add to an AI agent?

Genie Ontology is the governed context layer in Databricks. It supplies the definitions, relationships and source context an agent needs to interpret the business, such as the company's agreed activation metric. Organizations build that business meaning once and apply it across every agent connected to Genie.

Can Genie route questions to specialized Genie Agents?

Yes. For questions that need specialized analysis, Genie can route work to domain-specific Genie Agents. For example, a pipeline attribution question goes to the marketing Genie Agent and an operational cost question goes to the finance Genie Agent.

How do I get started with the Databricks Genie plugin?

Enable the Databricks Genie plugin in your agent workspace, then ask business questions or assign tasks to your agents in your normal workflow. Genie handles data retrieval and governance. In clients that support the MCP Apps extension, Genie also returns interactive visualizations and Genie Ontology citations in the conversation.
